interest: Shows SCAP's 1947 decision to liquidate, not reorganize, the Mitsui and Mitsubishi trading companies to curb postwar monopoly.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: Despatch transmits SCAPIN 1741 ordering liquidation of Mitsui Bussan and Mitsubishi Shoji, deemed too dangerous to reorganize since their trading networks could monopolize postwar foreign trade; strict rules bar former staff from reconstituting them.

people.name: R. M. Levy
people.role: Colonel, Adjutant General's Department, Adjutant General, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

people.name: Richard H. Bushner
people.role: Foreign Service Officer / Drafter, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of SCAPIN 1741 concerning the dissolution of the Mitsubishi and Mitsui trading companies, accompanied by commentary on SCAP's deconcentration strategy and antitrust policy.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan (drafted by Richard H. Bushner)
keywords: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: US Political Adviser forwards SCAPIN 1741 ordering Mitsui and Mitsubishi trading companies' liquidation to prevent postwar trade monopoly.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1163 from U.S. Political Adviser for Japan on SCAP Directive for Dissolution of Mitsubishi and Mitsui Trading Companies

subfiles.about: SCAP directive ordering the Japanese Government to immediately commence the dissolution and liquidation of the Mitsubishi and Mitsui trading companies under HCLC supervision.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (signed by Colonel R. M. Levy, Adjutant General)
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1741 orders Mitsui and Mitsubishi trading companies' liquidation, barring former staff from reconstituting them, reusing names, or large group re-employment, and requiring asset inventories and sales.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1741: Memorandum for the Japanese Government on Dissolution of Trading Companies
subfiles.to: Japanese Government (through Central Liaison Office, Tokyo)
